# Rights and delivery

For asset rights, credits, subtitles and delivery checks.

## Core

- Deliver a `CREDITS` file naming every third-party asset (samples, music, fonts, images, the voice engine) with its source and licence; credit on screen where a licence requires it; tell the user `CREDITS` lists the licences and the material is their responsibility.
- When anything is spoken, offer an `.srt` in one line.
- `voyager media review FILE` measures loudness but flags only a true peak above 0 dBTP (clipping): check `audio.integratedLUFS` near −14 and `audio.truePeakDBTP` at or below −1 yourself. It also checks black frames and duration. Re-level with two-pass `loudnorm` (`TP=-1`, `linear=true`, the first pass's measured values) and review again before presenting. When the audio is a person's recording, review the processed voice stem (not the final mix with music) and pass the recording as `--audio-source`: review then flags a noise floor raised more than 15 dB or crushed dynamics; never force a very quiet recording to the target.
- To judge continuous motion, sync or how a clip sounds, use a video-understanding model with `voyager models run`; load `choose-media-model/references/understanding.md` for the paid upload route.

# Composite a 3D object into footage in Blender

## Goal

{OBJECT} sits convincingly in {PLATE}: it follows the camera, matches light, haze and lens softness, and doesn't jitter. The original audio is kept. Everything stays editable (model, tracking data, render layers, composite) so a lost export can be rebuilt.

## How it came together

Read the shot before building: a stretch with open space for the object avoids rotoscoping, stable features make the track, and resolution, fps and cuts set the constraints. Agree placement and scale with the user first, and get the object's look approved on an isolated still lit to the plate's sun and fill.

For a distant object a 2D track (position, scale, rotation) on distant features was enough; a full camera solve is for real parallax. Measuring jitter, rather than eyeballing it, decided when the track was usable. The object rendered as a transparent sequence at its on-screen size and was composited over the untouched plate with matched colour, slight lens blur and haze added as colour. The user judged scale and placement on a full-res still.

The motion proof runs at source resolution and fps with original audio. Leftover head frames and one-frame pops hide at the start, around cuts, in the fastest motion and where a layer switches on. Extras (atmosphere, a build-in or fly-in, a look-dev pass) come after, each re-checked and shown. Ask before long renders.

## Example request

> Add a realistic {OBJECT} ({SIZE}, {FINISH}) to {PLATE} between {IN} and {OUT}. Place it {WHERE}, clear of {SUBJECTS}. Do it all in Blender and keep the original audio. Optional: {ATMOSPHERE / ANIMATION}.

## What worked in the original (starting points, not rules)

- A procedurally modelled airship over a bay in a 2.8 s shot; 8 shoreline markers, a smoothed 2D similarity track, Cycles CPU sprite renders at insert size (2-4 s/frame), VSE composite, optional volumetric clouds and a staged panel-by-panel build. No paid generation.

## Watch out for

- Raw per-frame track fits jitter visibly; smooth with consistent landmarks and measure the result.
- Faking distance by lowering opacity makes things see-through; composite opaque and add haze colour.
- Modifiers like Solidify can cause shading artefacts under hard light; bake and fix normals.
- First-pass atmosphere is usually too dense; thin it before showing.
- Warm key plus warm fill shifts metals' colour; keep the fill cool.
- Full-frame sprite renders waste time; render at on-screen size.
- In demos, don't pad short clips with frozen holds.
- If an export is lost and rebuilt from the editable layers, say it's a rebuild.
